headline: Chips Carry the Friday Tape as Software Names Split Sharply
body_html:
Midday Friday, the market is holding a slim but real advantage, with 295 names in our 545-stock universe trading higher against 247 lower. The dominant story is sector divergence: semiconductors are running the day, posting a sector gain of roughly 1.4% and standing well clear of every other group. Industrials and Materials are clinging to fractional advances, while Software, Consumer, Healthcare, and Energy all sit in the red — Healthcare off 0.42% and Energy the laggard at minus 0.49%.

The standout mover of the session is STAAR Surgical, up 7.6% and leading the healthcare-device space even as the broader healthcare sector struggles. MaxLinear has surged more than 7% in sympathy with the semiconductor theme, and Datadog — despite operating in a software space that is broadly under pressure — has climbed nearly 6.9%. Bloom Energy adds 5.3% on the energy side. Offsetting those gains, Zscaler has shed more than 8%, dragging cybersecurity peers lower, with Twilio off 6.7% and Okta down 3.7%.

Into the close, watch whether the semiconductor bid holds enough to keep the tape positive. A deterioration in breadth, already narrower than the headline numbers suggest, could tip the session. Geopolitical headlines around Iran and the broader Middle East corridor remain a background variable for energy and airline-exposed names.

briefs.headline: Zscaler Drags Cybersecurity Lower in Friday Selling
briefs.body: Zscaler is the session's biggest decliner, off more than 8% at midday, pulling peers including Qualys, down 3.1%, into the red alongside it. The move underscores a widening fault line within software, where security names are absorbing the bulk of the sector's 0.18% decline. Twilio and Okta are adding to the pressure on the broader software complex.

briefs.headline: Semiconductor Cohort Asserts Itself as Week Ends
briefs.body: The semiconductor sector is the clear leader Friday, posting a gain of roughly 1.4% against a mixed tape. MaxLinear is up more than 7% and Credo Technology has added nearly 4%, suggesting connectivity-focused chip names are carrying particular momentum. The move offers a counterweight to weakness spreading across consumer and healthcare segments.

briefs.headline: Iranian Flight Disruptions Deepen Across the Region
briefs.body: Three Iraqi airports have suspended flights connected to Iran starting Friday, adding to a growing pattern of aviation restrictions as the conflict around Iran continues. Qatar Airways has separately moved to retire idle wide-body jets and is redirecting pilot resources to partner carriers, reflecting the mounting operational toll of the prolonged hostilities on regional air networks.

briefs.headline: Oil Pulls Back as Truce Signals Temper Supply Fear
briefs.body: Crude prices are sliding Friday as market participants weigh hopes for a U.S.-Iran ceasefire against continued Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabian infrastructure. The tentative diplomatic signals appear to be outweighing the supply-disruption risk for now, contributing to Energy being the weakest sector on the day, off roughly 0.5%.

briefs.headline: Gold Firms on the Session but Faces a Losing Week
briefs.body: Gold is posting a modest intraday gain Friday but remains on course to log a weekly loss as expectations for further Federal Reserve rate increases continue to build. The combination of a firmer rate outlook and incremental geopolitical de-escalation signals has capped the metal's safe-haven bid through the back half of this week.

briefs.headline: Pharma Name Surges on High-Profile Injectables Agreement
briefs.body: A pharmaceutical company not in our covered universe has vaulted roughly 150% Friday after announcing a manufacturing deal tied to the injectable formulation of a well-known weight-loss therapy from Novo Nordisk. The move is drawing attention to contract manufacturing and specialty-injectables capacity as a theme, with Jabil — up nearly 4% — among the electronics-manufacturing names benefiting from related sentiment.
